podcast.body: This anthem was recorded on June 1, 1969, in room 1742 of the Queen Elizabeth Hotel in Montreal, during John Lennon and Yoko Ono's week-long bed-in for peace. André Perry, owner of a local recording studio, set up a simple four-microphone, four-track recorder system for the session. "on June 1st, 1969, in room 1742, the Anthem give peace a chance was recorded."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.body: This song was recorded live on June 1st, 1969, in room 1742 of the Queen Elizabeth Hotel in Montreal, during John and Yoko Ono's second "bed-in" peace protest. They invited guests like Tommy Smothers (on guitar), beat poet Allen Ginsberg, and Timothy Leary to participate. It quickly became a worldwide anthem for peace. "All we all say is give peace to chance. If it sounds like that they are banging on random things in a hotel room, they are."
